facts.fact: DGSN's Ismail Kdidar says the Mon e-ID platform has recorded 5,281,790 identity authentications since its launch on 25 April 2022, using the electronic ID card with PIN and facial recognition under law 04-20.
DGSN says 29 partner service providers use the Mon e-ID platform to authenticate users, including for the criminal record, nationality certificate and housing aid requests.
DGSN says citizens use the mobile application 'mon identité numérique' to prove their identity online and reach partners' digital services.

systems.platform: mobile app on the electronic ID card

MAR.note: No link between civil register and ID stated.

facts.fact: DGSN says users can use Mon e-ID to request the criminal record, the nationality certificate and housing aid online from partner service providers.

MAR.note: Three services named; no count of ten or more, no portal or usage figure.
Says every citizen has a physical ID card but gives no enrolment count or share.
Operation and maintenance of the ID system not stated.
No public register keyed on the ID number stated.

facts.fact: DGSN says every Moroccan citizen holds a physical identity based on the national identity card, from which a digital identity is derived.

MAR.note: Facial recognition is used to authenticate, not stated to stop double enrolment; no certification or audit.
Only ID authentication for criminal record requests and blockchain talk; no court case management system stated.
